def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # Identify uniform separator rows and columns.
    sep_rows = [r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1]
    sep_cols = [c for c in range(w) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1]

    # Keep only separator lines whose color forms the grid's repeated divider.
    div_color = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row), key=lambda x: sum(row.count(x) for row in grid))
    sep_rows = [r for r in sep_rows if grid[r][0] == div_color]
    sep_cols = [c for c in sep_cols if all(grid[r][c] == div_color for r in range(h))]

    rb = [0] + [r + 1 for r in sep_rows] + [h]
    cb = [0] + [c + 1 for c in sep_cols] + [w]
    row_ranges = [(rb[i], (sep_rows[i] if i < len(sep_rows) else h)) for i in range(len(rb))]
    col_ranges = [(cb[i], (sep_cols[i] if i < len(sep_cols) else w)) for i in range(len(cb))]

    regions = []
    for ri, (r0, r1) in enumerate(row_ranges):
        for ci, (c0, c1) in enumerate(col_ranges):
            if r0 < r1 and c0 < c1:
                regions.append((r0, r1, c0, c1))

    # Use the region with the most non-background cells as the repeating tile.
    bg = div_color
    src = max(regions, key=lambda q: sum(grid[r][c] != bg for r in range(q[0], q[1]) for c in range(q[2], q[3])))
    sr0, sr1, sc0, sc1 = src
    tile = [row[sc0:sc1] for row in grid[sr0:sr1]]

    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r0, r1 in row_ranges:
        for c0, c1 in col_ranges:
            if r0 >= r1 or c0 >= c1:
                continue
            for r in range(r0, r1):
                for c in range(c0, c1):
                    out[r][c] = tile[(r-r0) % len(tile)][(c-c0) % len(tile[0])]
    return out
